title: Incidents
description: Containers that crash-looped, exited repeatedly, ran out of memory, turned unhealthy or fired an alert — with everything McHarbor knows about them in one place.

detail.resolveDescription: Close the incident for {{name}} now and build its timeline. A new signal opens a new incident.

narrative.title: What happened
narrative.none: No narrative yet. Explain this sends the evidence below to the AI model configured for McHarbor.
narrative.undetermined: The model could not determine a cause from the available evidence. What it looked at is below.
narrative.shownHint: The exact, redacted text sent. Fingerprint {{hash}}.

refusal.not_opted_in: Narration is off for this environment. Turn it on in the narration settings first; nothing was sent.
refusal.no_model: No AI model is configured and enabled. Add one under the AI assistant settings; nothing was sent.
refusal.in_progress: A narration is already running for this incident.
refusal.cap_reached: The hourly narration limit for this environment is reached.
refusal.not_resolved: Only a resolved incident has a timeline to summarise.
refusal.model_failed: The model did not answer. The reason is on the incident.

pluginNote.plugin_unloaded: The plugin that raised this incident is not loaded, so its evidence could not be read.
pluginNote.plugin_unavailable: The plugin that raised this incident did not answer in time.

logsNote.unreachable: The environment could not be reached for logs.
logsNote.not_found: The container no longer exists, so there are no logs.
logsNote.logs_unavailable: The logs could not be read.

settings.title: Narration for this environment
settings.description: Whether incidents in this environment may be explained by the AI model, and how often.
settings.noModel: No AI model is configured and enabled, so nothing can be sent. Configure one under the AI assistant settings.
settings.destinationLocal: Evidence would go to {{connection}}: {{provider}} running {{model}} at {{url}}, a self-hosted model.
settings.destinationRemote: Evidence would leave this network: it goes to {{connection}}, {{provider}} running {{model}} at {{url}}.
settings.whatIsSent: What is sent: the container's recent events and log lines, image changes, audit entries and deploys touching it, alerts, drift and metrics — with passwords, tokens, credentials, addresses and Docker endpoints removed first. Environment variables are never sent.
settings.acknowledge: I understand that incident evidence from this environment will be sent to the model named above.
settings.hourlyCapHint: Automatic narration pauses once this many narrations have run in the last hour. Explain this is never refused for it.

snippet.title: Incident narrative
snippet.pending: An incident is open for this alert; no narrative yet.

findings.title: Behaviour findings
findings.description: Patterns found in the recorded history by fixed rules. The numbers are measured; a model may only explain them.

says.memory_climb: Memory grew {{growth}}% over {{days}} days, about {{perDay}} a day (fit {{r2}}).
says.host_memory_forecast: At {{current}}% and rising {{perDay}} points a day, memory is full in about {{days}} days.
says.scheduled_restarts: Restarts around {{time}} UTC on {{days}} different days.
says.post_deploy_failures: {{after}} failing exits in the day after a deploy, against {{before}} the day before.
says.host_disk_forecast: At {{current}}% and rising {{perDay}} points a day, this filesystem reaches {{ceiling}}% in about {{days}} days (fit {{r2}}).
says.storage_location_forecast: At {{current}}% and rising {{perDay}} points a day, this destination reaches {{ceiling}}% in about {{days}} days (fit {{r2}}).
